title: Stock Market Today Highlights, Nov 13: Markets snap 3-day rally; Sensex drops 318 points, Nifty slips below 25,150 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Business professional calculating financial interest growth by stacking gold coins with glowing percentage symbol and calculator on desk, representing investment return, interest rate strategy | Photo Credit: Shutthiphong Chandaeng

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 318.56 points, or 0.39%, to settle at 81,592.45. The 50-share NSE Nifty closed 155.05 points, or 0.61%, lower at 25,144.30.

Among the Sensex firms, Mahindra & Mahindra, UltraTech Cement, Bharat Electronics, NTPC, Trent and HDFC Bank were among the major laggards. Hindustan Unilever, Asian Paints, Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries were among the winners.

Retail inflation surged to 6.09% in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years and prompting economists to anticipate a policy rate hike by the central bank next month.

The consumer price index (CPI) based retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September, as a sustained uptick in food and beverages (F&B), restaurant services and transport inflation played a key role in pushing up the October headline number.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, remained flat at $95.76 per barrel.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.07 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it witnessed a high of 94.05 and a low of 94.28. The local unit settled at 94.20 (provisional), lower by 8 paise from its previous close.

Gillette India posts 10.8% quarterly profit rise to ₹159 crore as cost savings offset higher commodity costs; revenue up 4.4%.

Gem and jewellery exports increased 34 per cent last month to $2.92 billion against $2.18 logged in the same period last year.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.07 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it witnessed a high of 94.05 and a low of 94.28.

India's exports to the US rise 11% to $50.8 billion in April-September FY27 amid trade deal talks, while shipments to Africa and Asia also grow.

MAN Industries (India) Ltd, a leading manufacturer of large-diameter carbon steel line pipes, has reported a 121.7 per cent rise in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 82 crore during the September quarter.

The company had posted a PAT of Rs 37 crore in the year-ago period.

The revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,210 crore over Rs 834 crore in the year-ago period.

MAN Industries (India) Ltd, the flagship company of the MAN Group, was established in 1970 by the Mansukhani Family and has grown into one of India’s leading manufacturers and exporters of large-diameter carbon steel line pipes.

Following the acquisition of NPC, the company operates three manufacturing facilities at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh; Anjar, Gujarat; and Saudi Arabia, with a combined installed capacity of over 1.6 million MTPA. It supplies pipeline infrastructure to the oil and gas, petrochemicals, water transmission, fertilisers, dredging and city gas distribution sectors across India and global markets. (PTI)

India's gold imports fall 39.9% in April-October 2026, while the World Gold Council says the precious metal may be nearing a temporary price bottom.

India assures 75% import duty concession on bulk Scotch from Britain under its trade deal, amid a customs dispute over consignments held at ports.

Paytm gains preliminary RBI nod to issue prepaid wallets, sending shares to a record high after prior bans on wallet services.

Gaurav Gupta, President – India 2W Business, at TVS Motor Company, will step down from the company on December 24, 2026, to pursue an external opportunity.

Natco Pharma on Friday posted a 60.8 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 202.6 crore during the September quarter, weighed down by a fall in revenues.

The pharma company had reported a net profit of Rs 517.9 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal.

Its revenue from operations declined to Rs 967.3 crore in the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 1,363 crore a year ago, the company said in a regulatory filing.

Total expenses stood at Rs 776.2 crore, down from Rs 849.3 crore a year ago, it said.

During the quarter, Natco acquired an additional 13.25 per cent stake in Adcock Ingram Holding Ltd.

In the first half of the current fiscal (H1 FY27), Natco Pharma posted a 59 per cent decline in net profit to Rs 409.1 crore from Rs 998.2 crore in the April-September period of the preceding financial year.

The company’s board of directors also approved an interim dividend of Rs 1.25 per equity share of Rs 2 each during the quarter under review. (PTI)

Jagatjit Industries Ltd’s net loss has narrowed to Rs 3.96 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal, supported by higher revenue.

Its net loss stood at Rs 27.91 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income rose to Rs 195.43 crore in the July-September period of FY27 from Rs 103.11 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding year, according to a regulatory filing on Thursday.

During the first six months of the current financial year, the company’s net loss stood at Rs 12.23 crore, compared with Rs 37.81 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income grew to Rs 385.91 crore in the April-September period of the 2026-27 fiscal from Rs 233.62 crore in the corresponding period a year ago. (PTI)

Consumer watchdog says Ola’s tipping prompts misled users into believing additional payments could help secure rides faster.

KPI Green Energy reports Q2 FY2026-27 net profit at ₹92 cr, down 21%, as revenue rises 16% to ₹741 cr amid high depreciation and financing costs.

Aluminium prices fell marginally by Rs 2.20 to Rs 326.90 per kg in futures trade on Friday as participants trimmed their positions amid a weak trend in spot markets.

On the Multi Commodity Exchange, aluminium for delivery in November fell by Rs 2.20, or 0.67 per cent, to Rs 326.90 per kg in a business turnover of 3,410 lots.
